# SPECS & IA: The New Software Development Cycle (Specification as Dialogue)

The video shows how AI changes specification-guided development (SDD): the specification ceases to be a rigid contract and becomes a live dialogue. It has three levels of specification, the cycle of collaboration with AI, the use in legacy code and the new skills of those who develop.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on December 3, 2025 (6 min 56 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jcFFT-W1vE4

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## Specification is not back to the waterfall

With AI assistants to program, specification-guided development (SDD) has returned, but in a new way [00:00].

Fear is that writing specifications is a setback to the cascade model, in which everything was written in stone before the first line of code [00:20].

The turn is to rethink what a specification is. Before, it was a strict contract, and changing in the middle of the way was a flaw in planning. With the AI, the spec is a living dialogue: it evolves, and change is learning [00:40].

The goal is not to freeze the future, but to make clear the intention of the moment [01:01].

According to the video, in modern SDD the specification is a living document, the source of truth that evolves with the project and guides directly what the AI implements. Thus, people and AI are aligned all the time [02:03].

## A menu of specifications

There is not a single way to specify. The level of detail depends on the task [02:03]:

- **Level 1, intention:** for quick changes, like a bug or a new button. It says why and what [02:25].
- **Level 2, iterative plan:** for most features, as a new login. Defines the technical strategy without the stiffness of the cascade [02:25].
- **Level 3, blueprint:** for high-risk systems, such as the core of a banking system. Uses formal logic [02:47].

Agility is in choosing the right level for each work [02:47].

## The Golden Cycle

Work is a constant collaboration between those who develop and the AI agent [03:09]:

1. begins with intent [03:09];
2. the AI proposes a plan [03:09];
3. the person reviews the plan before any code is generated [03:09];
4. the adjustment goes back to the specification [03:31];
5. with corrected spec, the AI implements again [03:31].

The golden rule is: do not correct the code, correct the specification [03:31]. Thus, the documentation and system never separate, and the manual does not differ from the software that runs [03:52].

## AI as legacy code archaeologist

In legacy systems, SDD may show its highest value: AI acts as software archaeologist, and the flow becomes code, spec, code [04:14].

The AI analyzes the code to understand what it actually does, not what the old documentation says. Then it generates a specification of current behavior that people validate and refine. With this map, you can refactor without fear of breaking everything [04:35].

The memory of the application does not disappear when someone leaves the company: the knowledge that was in people's heads becomes a documented asset [04:56].

## New Skills

Requirements engineering, previously seen as bureaucracy, becomes one of the most valuable skills on the team [04:56].

According to the video, the key skills are [05:19]:

- instrument design: requirements so precise that they function as a scalpel in the hand of the AI [05:19];
- contextualization: give the AI the map of the project [05:19];
- testability of all that is asked [05:40];
- reduction of ambiguity: whoever develops becomes a curator of clarity [05:40].

## Trails, not walls

The change is from heavy and prescriptive documentation to useful and iterative guidance. The AI does not require more bureaucracy, but useful documentation: the quality of guidance matters more than the number of pages [06:02].

The specifications are not walls that limit creativity, but tracks that guide the AI and the team with speed and predictability [06:23].

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is SDD a spin on the cascade model?

Nope. According to the video, the specification becomes a live dialogue that evolves, not a rigid contract [00:40].

### What do you do when AI goes wrong?

Correct specification, not code. Thus, the documentation and the system do not separate [03:31].

## About the video

Will Artificial Intelligence Kill Spec Guided Development (SDD)? 
In this essential video, we demystify the relationship between Specifications (Specs) and Artificial Intelligence, showing how AI does not lead us back to the cascade model, but transforms specs into a flexible and iterative dialogue. If you are a Developer, Software Architect or Product Manager, this content is crucial for the future of your career.
What you'll learn:
Specs as Chat: As the specifications evolve from rigid contracts to tracks that guide the AI, reducing ambiguity.
The Human-IA Gold Cycle: A collaborative workflow where the focus is to correct the specification, not the code, ensuring that documentation and software are always synchronized.
Software Archaeology with AI: Find out how AI can be used to rescue knowledge into legacy codes, transforming development.
New Essential Skills: Understand the importance of "tool design" and the reduction of ambiguity for the modern developer.
The future of development is collaborative. Watch now and get ready to master the new software creation paradigm with the AI!
